messages.content: " * Print the help for options with the specified * command line syntax. * * @param pw the writer to which the help will be written * @param width the number of characters to be displayed on each line * @param cmdLineSyntax the syntax for this application * @param header the banner to display at the begining of the help * @param options the Options instance * @param leftPad the number of characters of padding to be prefixed * to each line * @param descPad the number of characters of padding to be prefixed * to each description line * @param footer the banner to display at the end of the help * * @throws IllegalStateException if there is no room to print a line "

The failing test `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored` is testing the `HelpFormatter` class in the Apache Commons CLI library. The test sets up an `Options` object and adds an option with a long description. Then it creates a `HelpFormatter` instance, prints the help with a width of 22 characters per line, and compares the generated help output to an expected string.

The current bug report describes an issue where the `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop if there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, leading to a JVM crash with an `OutOfMemoryError`.

By looking at the `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class, it is evident that this method is responsible for formatting and printing the help for the provided options. The method takes parameters such as the writer, width, command line syntax, header, options, paddings, and footer.

Based on the failing test and the bug report, it seems that the issue lies within the logic of wrapping long words in the help output when there is not enough space. This could potentially lead to an infinite loop trying to wrap the word, consuming excessive memory until the JVM crashes.

To address this issue, the logic for word wrapping and handling long descriptions in the `printHelp` method of the `HelpFormatter` class needs to be reviewed and fixed to prevent the infinite looping behavior.

Considering the symptoms and the code snippet of the `printHelp` method, here is a likely diagnosis:

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The `HelpFormatter` class in the Apache Commons CLI library has a bug in the word wrapping logic within the `printHelp` method. When there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, the method goes into an infinite loop, leading to an `OutOfMemoryError` and JVM crash. This behavior is triggered when formatting long descriptions in the help output. The issue resides in the handling of word wrapping and line-length calculation within the `printHelp` method.

Given the symptoms and the code snippet, the root cause of the issue is likely the incorrect word wrapping logic in the `printHelp` method of the `HelpFormatter` class.

Suggestions for fixing:
```java
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter,int,java.lang.String,java.lang.String,org.apache.commons.cli.Options,int,int,java.lang.String)
```
